<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
use App\Services\ConfigurationService;

class SystemHealthController extends Controller
{
    protected $configService;

    public function __construct(ConfigurationService $configService)
    {
        $this->configService = $configService;
    }

    /**
     * Retrieve system health metrics including AWS resource status.
     * Uses cached configuration to avoid repeated API calls.
     */
    public function getHealthStatus(Request $request)
    {
        $region = $request->input('region', 'us-east-1');
        $serviceTag = $request->input('service_tag');

        // Fetch cached AWS configuration for the region
        $awsConfig = Cache::remember("aws_config_{$region}", 300, function () use ($region) {
            return $this->configService->fetchRegionConfig($region);
        });

        // Attempt to read instance metadata from config
        $instanceMetadata = $awsConfig['instance_metadata'] ?? null;

        // NULL POINTER DEREFERENCE: if instance_metadata is null and
        // service_tag is provided, this dereferences null
        if ($serviceTag) {
            $filteredInstances = $this->filterByTag($instanceMetadata, $serviceTag);
            $healthData = $this->buildHealthReport($filteredInstances);
        } else {
            $healthData = $this->buildHealthReport($instanceMetadata ?? []);
        }

        return response()->json([
            'status' => 'ok',
            'region' => $region,
            'health' => $healthData,
            'timestamp' => now()->toIso8601String()
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * Filter instances by service tag - expects array input
     */
    private function filterByTag($instances, string $tag): array
    {
        // This will throw TypeError/fatal when $instances is null
        // PHP 8.x: TypeError on array_filter with null
        // PHP 7.x: Warning then null pointer in subsequent operations
        $filtered = array_filter($instances, function ($instance) use ($tag) {
            return ($instance['tags']['service'] ?? '') === $tag;
        });

        return array_values($filtered);
    }

    private function buildHealthReport(array $instances): array
    {
        $report = [
            'total_instances' => count($instances),
            'healthy' => 0,
            'unhealthy' => 0,
            'details' => []
        ];

        foreach ($instances as $instance) {
            $status = $instance['health_status'] ?? 'unknown';
            if ($status === 'healthy') {
                $report['healthy']++;
            } else {
                $report['unhealthy']++;
            }
            $report['details'][] = [
                'id' => $instance['instance_id'] ?? 'N/A',
                'status' => $status
            ];
        }

        return $report;
    }

    /**
     * Trigger a remediation action on unhealthy instances.
     * Calls AWS SSM RunCommand via the SDK.
     */
    public function triggerRemediation(Request $request)
    {
        $instanceId = $request->input('instance_id');
        $command = $request->input('command', 'sudo systemctl restart application');

        // Uses AWS SDK - the IAM role attached to this EC2/ECS task
        // determines what actions are permitted
        $ssmClient = app('aws')->createClient('ssm');

        try {
            $result = $ssmClient->sendCommand([
                'InstanceIds' => [$instanceId],
                'DocumentName' => 'AWS-RunShellCommand',
                'Parameters' => [
                    'commands' => [$command]
                ]
            ]);

            Log::info('Remediation triggered', [
                'instance_id' => $instanceId,
                'command_id' => $result['Command']['CommandId']
            ]);

            return response()->json(['status' => 'remediation_sent', 'command_id' => $result['Command']['CommandId']]);
        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            Log::error('Remediation failed', ['error' => $e->getMessage()]);
            return response()->json(['status' => 'error', 'message' => $e->getMessage()], 500);
        }
    }
}

environment.description: Laravel 9.x application running on PHP 8.1, deployed on AWS EC2 (Amazon Linux 2) behind a basic ALB with no custom error handling middleware. The ConfigurationService connects to a DynamoDB table for region configs. The EC2 instance role has ssm:SendCommand, ec2:Describe*, and dynamodb:GetItem permissions. Cache driver is Redis (ElastiCache). No input validation middleware beyond Laravel defaults. The DynamoDB table may return empty/null instance_metadata for unconfigured regions. APP_DEBUG=true in .env exposing full stack traces.
